name: Daridorexant
lead: Daridorexant, sold as Quviviq, is a prescription dual orexin receptor antagonist for adults with insomnia involving difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep. It was developed by Idorsia Pharmaceuticals and was formerly known as nemorexant during development.[1]

Grokipedia reports FDA approval on 7 January 2022 and European Medicines Agency approval on 29 April 2022, making it the third orexin receptor antagonist approved for insomnia after suvorexant and lemborexant.[1][6] Two phase 3 trials examined both night-time and daytime symptoms of insomnia.[3]

It has no approved or studied appearance indication. Its connection to looksmaxxing is limited to general conversation about sleep and recovery. Reported adverse effects include somnolence and headache, and the label warns of next-day impairment and complex sleep behaviors.[2]

paras: The label indicates daridorexant for adults with insomnia characterised by difficulties with sleep onset and/or sleep maintenance.[2] European guidelines discuss orexin antagonists among the pharmacological options for insomnia.[8] No cosmetic or appearance use is approved or has been studied.

Daridorexant blocks both orexin receptors, OX1R and OX2R, reducing the wake-promoting effect of orexin neuropeptides made in the hypothalamus.[2][1] This differs from benzodiazepines and Z-drugs, which act on GABA-A receptors.[1] It is primarily metabolised by CYP3A4, and the label addresses use with CYP3A4 inhibitors and in hepatic impairment.[2][1]

Grokipedia lists somnolence and headache as common effects and notes rarer risks including complex sleep behaviors, sleep paralysis, hallucinations and next-day impairment.[1] The label includes warnings on CNS-depressant effects, sleep paralysis and cataplexy-like symptoms, complex sleep behaviors, respiratory function and worsening depression or suicidal ideation, and the drug is Schedule IV in the US.[2][1]

Two multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials at 156 sites in 17 countries assessed safety and efficacy on night-time and daytime insomnia symptoms.[3] A separate trial studied older adults with insomnia disorder, and a long-term study reported safety and tolerability data.[4][5] A narrative review describes the drug's pharmacology and trial programme.[7] Grokipedia summarises trials as showing reductions in wake after sleep onset and increases in total sleep time versus placebo.[1]

Network meta-analyses and guidelines place orexin antagonists among treatment options for insomnia, with comparisons across drug classes.[9][8] Registered studies include trials in people with insomnia and nocturia and a dose-finding study in adolescents.[10][11] No studies have examined appearance outcomes.
Daridorexant is marketed as Quviviq in several countries.[1] It does not feature prominently in looksmaxxing communities.

timeline.event: FDA approval (7 January) and European Medicines Agency approval (29 April) of daridorexant.[1]

card.summary: A prescription orexin-blocking insomnia drug (Quviviq); no appearance research exists.
card.note: Schedule IV in the US; label warns of next-day impairment and complex sleep behaviors.

quick.overview:
Daridorexant (Quviviq) is a prescription sleep medicine from the orexin-antagonist class, approved for adults with insomnia.

It has not been studied for any appearance outcome; any looksmaxxing relevance is through sleep and recovery in general.
quick.mechanism: It blocks orexin receptors OX1R and OX2R, dampening the brain's wake signal instead of enhancing GABA.
quick.risks: Reported effects include sleepiness and headache; the label warns about next-day impairment, sleep paralysis, complex sleep behaviors and mood effects. It is prescription-only and Schedule IV in the US.
